segments: The 11th period.
Arab kings.
the monks,
and burned their ladders with naphtha.
Then the Kurds cut away a section from the mountain above the monastery,
and rolled it down upon it.
And that great rock split into two:
one part breached the wall,
and remained in that breach like a seal in a ring, without budging.
And the other part pierced through the wall,
and passed into it.
And the Kurds came to enter,
but the monks and the people of the countryside who were refugees there gathered together,
and fought with stones and arrows,
and did not let them enter.
And they rebuilt the breach with stones and plaster right at that hour.
And in these battles, one eye of the abbot Abu Nasr was gouged out,
and a few men were struck by arrows,
but they were helped again.
And when the monks grew weary of battle,
they sought peace from the Kurds,
and agreed to give them all the property and treasures of the church,
and also to collect for them gold, silver, and ornaments from the people of the countryside.
The Kurds, however,
because they had heard the report of the coming of the Tatars, quickly inclined to peace,
and took much wealth from the monastery,
the value of which amounted to a thousand gold dinars,
and departed.
And at that time,
the people of the village of Beth Sahraye and others of the people of Nineveh,
while they were shut up in the Monastery of the Cell-dwellers {OCR?},
set out from there,
and went and crossed the Zab River to go to Erbil.
And Qutlu-beg the emir met them,
and made an accusation against them,
saying, "They come from the side of the enemies."
And he killed them all,
men and women alike.
And 'Alam Sanjar,
as soon as he entered Mosul,
heard that the Tatars had come from the region of Jazira,
and went out, met them, and was killed.
And a scout of the Tatars came,
and informed them, "Behold, al-Malik al-Salih is coming again to Mosul."
And because of this, the Tatars stayed overnight and did not come against Mosul,
until that Salih came and entered it.
Now Sayf al-Din, the lord of Jazira, when he heard
that Salih his brother had fled to Syria,
prepared to flee himself as well.
